result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A fits the flat, blunt brand more closely. It uses a single zero radius and makes state changes instant by default, with one optional 120ms duration and no easing tokens. It also says plainly what is left out (radius scales, soft shadows, easing) and treats the hard offset shadow as a brand decision for the user to make. Answer B is concrete and its offset elevation scale and press-collapse idea are good, but it adds a cubic-bezier easing, a 200ms duration for drawers and a 50% radius exception, so it drifts toward a conventional system. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B fits the flat, blunt brand more closely. It keeps a single zero radius with no ladder, builds depth from rules, z-index and a flat scrim, defaults motion to instant with no easing tokens, and says plainly which tokens it leaves out and why. A is also strong and very concrete, but it adds a 50% radius exception, a second duration and two easing curves, and says less about what the system leaves out.
